analysis.investment_thesis: Electrosteel Castings fails both legs of the Magic Formula: earnings yield is only ~6–7% (EV/EBITDA of 15.09x implies EBIT/EV well below my 12% threshold) and ROCE of 13.4% is meaningfully below the 20% minimum for a "good business." With operating margin at -0.71% and forward P/E (35.11x) nearly 2.5× the trailing P/E (14.20x), the market is pricing in a severe earnings collapse — not the durable, high-ROIC compounder the Magic Formula demands.
key_strengths: Long-term revenue CAGR of 14.3% (2016–2025) with dominant DI pipe position tied to India's Jal Jeevan Mission infrastructure spending
Debt actively deleveraging — total debt down from INR 2,967 Cr (FY22) to INR 2,125 Cr (FY25), D/E now only 0.38x
Trading below book value (P/B 0.84x) with 50.14% promoter holding, limiting downside risk
key_risks: Forward P/E of 35.11x vs trailing 14.20x implies standalone earnings falling ~60% — a catastrophic signal Greenblatt's formula cannot tolerate
Operating margin of -0.71% means the standalone operating business is losing money; net profits are propped by other income/consolidated subsidiaries
Poor FCF conversion: FY25 FCF only INR 206 Cr vs net profit of INR 710 Cr (29% conversion), with capex rising to INR 278 Cr and CWIP still elevated at INR 1,186 Cr
red_flags: Forward P/E (35.11x) vastly exceeds trailing P/E (14.20x) — signals expected earnings collapse, not growth
Negative operating margin (-0.71%) on a standalone basis; Magic Formula requires positive, durable EBIT
Earnings history is deeply erratic: net losses in FY16, FY21; OCF went negative in FY22 (-279 Cr); not the stable, high-ROIC business the formula targets
Revenue has stalled: INR 7,276 Cr → 7,478 Cr → 7,320 Cr over last 3 years — the growth engine is sputtering
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Through the Magic Formula lens, Electrosteel Castings scores poorly on both required dimensions. Back-solving from EV/EBITDA of 15.09x and market cap of INR 4,997 Cr (EV ~INR 7,070 Cr), implied standalone EBITDA is ~INR 468 Cr. Stripping depreciation, EBIT/EV (earnings yield) comes in at roughly 6–7% — well below my 12% attractiveness threshold and nowhere near the 15%+ I need to get excited. ROCE of 13.4% similarly fails the 20% hurdle for a "good business." A company can be cheap OR good; this one is neither.

The consolidated income statement flatters the picture: consolidated EBITDA was INR 1,149 Cr in FY25, but the listed entity's standalone economics are far weaker, as evidenced by the -0.71% operating margin and the forward P/E implying earnings near INR 142 Cr versus ~INR 352 Cr trailing. FCF conversion of just 29% (INR 206 Cr FCF on INR 710 Cr net profit) and rising capex (INR 278 Cr in FY25) confirm this is a capital-intensive, cyclical business with lumpy earnings — precisely the type the Magic Formula is designed to avoid. The infrastructure tailwind is real, but a good macro story does not compensate for poor unit economics at the business level.
